In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the stability properties of QDMC with constraints depend on the choice of the weighting matrices in the objective function, the constraints, and the sampling time.
the stability of the nonlinear closed-loop system can be guaranteed by a proper choice of the degree of softening of the constraints, which depends on the degree of constraint violation.

the presence of constraints in MPC does not imply instability of the closed loop system, and that stability of the closed-loop system can be ensured by appropriate choice of the softening of constraints and of the prediction horizon.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the closed-loop stability of QDMC can be guaranteed by a proper choice of constraints.
the presence of soft constraints in the optimization problem solved by QDMC results in a closed loop stable system, provided that the constraints are not too soft.
the stability of constrained QDMC can be guaranteed by a suitable choice of the control horizon and by a proper tuning of the weighting factors in the objective function.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in the presence of constraints, it is important to consider the closed-loop system as a whole, and not to focus only on the nominal system, as it is usually the case.
the stability analysis of constrained nonlinear control systems can be reduced to the stability analysis of a linear system with a single constraint on the control variable.
, in the presence of constraints, the closed-loop stability of a constrained MPC system cannot be determined by the open-loop stability of the unconstrained system.
